title: Replace lost brain tissue while preserving learned function

concept.text: Conceptual synthesis: The innovation would replace lost brain tissue with living cells that become useful parts of existing neural circuits. Replacement neurons would need to survive, develop appropriate identities, connect with suitable partners and contribute to meaningful function while preserving the person's retained learned abilities. The goal is functional repair, rather than cell survival alone.

Scope clarification: Restoring a damaged circuit's useful operation does not necessarily require reconstructing every original connection. However, restoring a function and recovering the particular information once stored in destroyed tissue are different achievements. This concept includes preserving retained learning during tissue replacement; it does not assume that replacement cells can recreate lost individual memories or restore identity after extensive tissue loss.

significance.text: Conditional significance: If replacement tissue could integrate safely and restore complex function, some lasting consequences of brain damage could become repairable. The revolutionary advance would be the ability to rebuild functional biological capacity after tissue loss, with recovery that extends beyond keeping transplanted cells alive. The supplied material does not establish which injuries, affected functions or patients would benefit.

Conditional downstream possibilities: Successful repair across different forms of focal damage could support a broader approach to brain reconstruction. Its reach would still depend on the amount and location of tissue lost, the condition of surviving circuits and the continuing disease or injury environment. Reconstructing specific lost memories or aspects of identity would require additional breakthroughs; it does not follow from graft integration or improved clinical function.

missing_breakthrough.text: Scientific synthesis: The missing capability is dependable replacement tissue that participates appropriately in established brain circuits while preserving retained learned function. The candidate identifies several linked barriers: transplanted neurons must survive, acquire suitable cellular identities, connect with appropriate partners and operate safely in the recipient's disease or injury environment. These are coherent engineering requirements, but the supplied accessible source material does not independently substantiate their technical details or show that they have been solved together.

Scientific synthesis: Useful connectivity must produce appropriate circuit behavior, rather than merely anatomical connections or detectable activity. Repair must also accommodate surviving circuitry without disrupting abilities it already supports. Demonstrating that replacement tissue contributes to recovery is a separate challenge from observing improvement after transplantation: recovery could otherwise reflect changes in surviving tissue, rehabilitation or other concurrent treatment.

Safety and information limits: The proposed capability must address abnormal growth, seizures, immune effects and deterioration over time. Preserving learned abilities also creates an information constraint: retained knowledge must remain usable as circuits change, while information destroyed with lost tissue cannot be assumed to reappear simply because new cells occupy the damaged region. The supplied material provides no demonstrated solution to these combined problems.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a paper titled “Phase I trial of hES cell-derived dopaminergic neurons for Parkinson’s disease,” attributed to Tabar and colleagues and dated 16 April 2025. It reports an open-label phase I study in which 12 participants received stem-cell-derived dopamine neuron progenitors and immunosuppression, with survival imaging and exploratory clinical assessments. According to that research account, the study met its one-year safety objectives and imaging was consistent with graft survival. These are reported trial details whose underlying text could not be verified in the supplied review.

The access limitation materially constrains interpretation. Although the research says an abstract was inspected, the review found that the retained artifact contained only a cookie notice, with no abstract, methods or results. Its content therefore could not confirm the intended document's identity, participant count, study design, safety findings or imaging findings. The source index's saved and verified flags, and its indication that extraction was not truncated, do not establish that scientific content was captured. This limitation leaves the reported findings unverified here; it is not evidence that they are false.

Methodological interpretation: If the reported study details are accurate, they would describe a narrower advance in dopamine-cell replacement for Parkinson’s disease. An uncontrolled study cannot by itself establish treatment efficacy, and imaging consistent with graft survival does not establish reconstruction of complex learned circuits or preservation of retained learned abilities. Meeting one-year safety objectives would also have a defined observation window; it would not settle longer-term safety. Even a verified result of this kind would not demonstrate restoration after two distinct forms of focal brain damage.

Evidence boundary: No bounded search record or freshness entries were supplied, so the material cannot establish whether later developments changed the field through 1 November 2026, the review's stated freshness cutoff. The supplied evidence therefore supports neither a comprehensive account of current progress nor a conclusion that the full innovation has been achieved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Controlled trials would show durable restoration of meaningful functions after at least two distinct forms of focal brain damage, with evidence that integrated replacement tissue contributes to recovery. Assessments would explicitly test preservation of retained learned abilities, aligning the demonstration with the concept's title. The two-damage requirement is a proposed test of breadth, not an established scientific standard.
completion_criteria.label: Durable recovery after two damage types preserves retained learning

completion_criteria.text: Proposed study requirements: Investigators would specify meaningful functional outcomes, durability periods, comparison conditions and safety monitoring periods in advance. Evidence would connect graft integration to functional contribution, rather than relying solely on cell survival, imaging or improvement after treatment. Assessments of retained learning would distinguish preservation of existing abilities from newly acquired compensatory strategies.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified assessments link graft integration to function and retained learning

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: Convincing results would be reproducible in independent cohorts and, where feasible, across clinical teams. Long-term follow-up would address abnormal growth, seizures, immune effects and deterioration, while defining the injuries, tissue-loss extent, recipient conditions and accompanying treatments under which benefit was demonstrated. Successful finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not universal repairability of brain damage or recovery of all lost memories.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication documents long-term safety outcomes and demonstrated benefit boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based scope comparison: NRL-04, “Read and selectively repair the physical traces of specific memories,” concerns particular stored memories. NRL-06 concerns replacement tissue and broader functional recovery, including preservation of retained learning. The two overlap when repair affects memory-bearing circuits, but successful tissue replacement would not by itself demonstrate selective memory reconstruction. This comparison uses the supplied titles and candidate's scope description; no full NRL-04 record was provided.

Roster-based scope comparison: NRL-05, “Regenerate a severely injured spinal cord with functional reconnection,” and NRL-16, “Biologically repair the injured visual pathway,” share the objective of biological repair with useful reconnection. Their anatomical and functional targets differ from replacing lost brain tissue. NRL-02, a predictive theory of neural circuit computation, and NRL-03, cellular-resolution whole-brain recording during natural behavior, could inform the design or assessment of replacement circuits, but neither capability alone constitutes tissue repair.

Roster-based scope comparison: NRL-13 concerns protecting brain tissue during acute ischemic stroke, whereas NRL-06 addresses replacement after loss. NRL-09 concerns preventing Alzheimer’s dementia before irreversible functional loss; NRL-11 concerns halting established Alzheimer’s disease and restoring lost function. Tissue replacement could overlap with the restorative part of NRL-11, but integration of a graft would not by itself establish control of the underlying disease. NRL-15's focus on shared mechanisms of neurodegeneration and NRL-18's focus on the disease process associated with chronic traumatic encephalopathy likewise concern processes that could affect the environment in which repair must operate.

Roster-based scope comparison: NRL-10's programmable delivery to selected brain cells could be an enabling capability, while NRL-14's seizure-control objective intersects with a major safety concern for circuit repair. NRL-12 concerns immune control and remyelination, a distinct form of repair. NRL-07, NRL-08 and NRL-17 concern neural communication or prosthetic interfaces that could restore useful capabilities without demonstrating replacement of lost tissue. NRL-01's theory of consciousness addresses a separate explanatory objective; functional graft integration would not resolve consciousness or establish preservation of identity.

unresolved_issues: The intended paper's identity and reported trial details remain unverified from the retained artifact; an inspectable abstract or full scientific text would be needed to resolve them.
The supplied material does not establish efficacy, reconstruction of complex learned circuits or preservation of retained learned abilities following transplantation.
Which injuries, tissue-loss extents and disease environments could support effective replacement remains unresolved.
Clinically meaningful outcome thresholds, durability periods and long-term monitoring windows remain to be specified; the proposed criteria are not presented as consensus standards.
No supplied search record establishes subsequent developments through 1 November 2026 or a comprehensive present-day account.
Related-concept comparisons are limited to the supplied roster titles and the candidate's NRL-04 description; fuller records could refine their boundaries.

brief.title: Brain tissue repair that preserves learned abilities
possible: People who have lost brain tissue could regain useful abilities through living replacement cells that join surviving brain circuits, the networks of connected nerve cells. Repair would preserve abilities they still have as new tissue becomes part of the brain.
why: Some lasting effects of brain damage could become repairable. For affected people, recovery would mean rebuilding the brain’s capacity to function, beyond simply keeping transplanted cells alive.

sources.showed: In an early safety trial, 12 people with Parkinson’s disease received replacement nerve cells grown from stem cells. The trial met its initial safety goals, and brain scans indicated that transplanted cells survived.
sources.quote: The trial achieved its primary objectives of safety and tolerability one year after transplantation, with no adverse events related to the cell product.
sources.cited_for: Replacement nerve cells have reached human safety trials.
sources.not_established: The trial had no control group and did not establish treatment effectiveness or preservation of learned abilities.

sources.who: Sara Palma-Tortosa, Daniel Tornero and colleagues
sources.showed: Human nerve cells formed connections in stroke-injured rat brains and influenced movement. Transplantation corrected uneven forelimb use, but silencing the cells did not bring that particular impairment back.
sources.quote:
We show that the stroke-induced
asymmetry in a sensorimotor (cylinder) test is reversed by trans-
plantation.
sources.cited_for: Transplanted cells can join damaged brain circuits and influence behavior.
sources.not_established: The corrected forelimb imbalance did not depend on ongoing activity in the transplanted cells, and retained learning was not established.

sources.who: Dennis Jgamadze, Han-Chiao Isaac Chen and colleagues
sources.showed: Human brain organoids, small tissues grown from stem cells, connected with the visual system in injured adult rat brains. Their nerve cells responded to visual stimulation, including the orientation of what the rats saw.
sources.quote: Visual stimulation of host animals elicits responses in organoid neurons, including orientation selectivity.
sources.cited_for: Replacement tissue can receive and process sensory signals within an injured adult brain.
sources.not_established: Responses to visual stimulation do not establish restored useful vision or preservation of learned abilities.

sources.showed: Human cells that develop into nerve cells improved walking and fine movement in stroke-injured mice. The treatment also reduced inflammation and supported repair of surrounding tissue.
sources.quote: NPC-treated mice show improved gait and fine-motor recovery, as quantified by deep learning-based analysis.
sources.cited_for: Cell transplants can support movement recovery and repair responses after stroke in mice.
sources.not_established: Improvement does not establish that replacement circuits caused recovery or preserved retained learning.

sources.showed: In rats with Parkinson-like damage, researchers could increase or reduce the benefit of transplanted nerve cells by controlling their activity. They also identified a mechanism that caused unwanted movements.
sources.quote:
With this model, we demonstrate unequivocally that
an active DA neurotransmission is necessary for the therapeutic
capacity of the fetal graft.
sources.cited_for: Changing transplanted cells’ activity can test whether those cells contribute to recovery.
sources.not_established: This movement-repair model does not establish reconstruction of complex learned circuits or preservation of existing abilities.

shown: Tabar and colleagues have tested replacement nerve cells in people with Parkinson’s disease. In rats, Palma-Tortosa and colleagues showed that transplanted human nerve cells influence movement, while Jgamadze and colleagues showed that transplanted brain tissue responds to visual signals.
missing: Replacement cells still need to survive, develop suitable identities and make useful connections together reliably.
Controlled human trials have yet to show lasting functional repair while preserving previously learned abilities.
Recovery must be traced to replacement tissue rather than surviving tissue, rehabilitation or accompanying treatment.
Long-term safety must address abnormal growth, seizures, immune effects and declining function.

milestones.label: Lasting recovery across two damage types preserves learned abilities
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show lasting recovery after two distinct types of localized brain damage, with replacement tissue contributing and retained learning preserved. This would demonstrate breadth and useful repair.

milestones.label: Planned assessments connect replacement tissue to preserved function
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to set outcomes, comparisons and follow-up periods beforehand, link transplanted tissue to function, and distinguish retained learning from compensation. This would establish what the repair actually achieves.

milestones.label: Independent studies establish lasting safety and limits of benefit
milestones.explanation: Independent groups would have to reproduce benefits, track long-term harms and define which injuries, tissue losses and treatment conditions allow recovery. This would establish where repair works safely.

uncertain: Which injuries, amounts of tissue loss and continuing disease conditions can support useful replacement remains unresolved.
Meaningful recovery thresholds and follow-up periods remain unsettled; the proposed milestones are not agreed scientific standards.
Preserving surviving knowledge differs from recovering destroyed memories; new cells cannot be assumed to recreate lost information.

page.title: Neuronal replacement with preservation of learned function
page.definition: Living replacement neurons join surviving brain circuits and help restore a function lost to injury or neurodegeneration. A person may need to relearn the lost skill. Preservation concerns skills the person could still perform just before transplantation and can still perform afterward. Japan has conditionally approved raguneprocel, a graft of immature dopamine-producing nerve cells, for a limited period for Parkinson’s motor symptoms inadequately controlled by medication. Preservation of learned skills remains a separate question.

goal.need: More than 20 million US adults are estimated to live with chronic damage to the neocortex after stroke, trauma or neurodegeneration. Physical and speech therapy can improve function, but people with severe damage often depend on caregivers. Replacing lost neurons could help someone regain speech, vision or control of movement while keeping skills they still use in daily life. Recovery may still require practice specific to the lost skill.

statements.body: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, FRONT programme
statements.quote: The Functional Repair of Neocortical Tissue (FRONT) program aims to restore brain tissue, enabling individuals with brain damage to recover cognitive functions.
the goal is to deliver dopamine producing cells to replace the lost neurons
statements.context: A statement about a funded preclinical dopamine-cell replacement project for Parkinson’s disease.

completion.title: A human neuronal graft restores impaired function while preserving retained learned abilities.
completion.criterion: In one defined clinical indication, a controlled human trial meets prespecified endpoints for restoration of an impaired function and preservation of abilities learned and retained before transplantation, with evidence that graft-derived neurons contribute to the restored circuit. Preservation is demonstrated against a clinically justified margin relative to baseline and controls, rather than inferred from a nonsignificant decline. Benefits and graft safety meet the trial’s prespecified follow-up requirements.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external combined criterion located.
completion.basis: The ISSCR calls for controlled evidence of effectiveness. FRONT measures reacquisition of a learned task in animals. Japan’s conditional approval of raguneprocel concerns Parkinson’s motor symptoms and requires further efficacy assessment. A sham-controlled trial of fetal dopamine grafts compared cognitive performance before surgery and one year later. Its nonsignificant group difference does not bound the amount of decline compatible with the data. The combined test and its requirement for a justified preservation margin are Atlas criteria.

milestones.title: Grafted neurons increase firing when the host receives sensory stimulation.
milestones.criterion: Record electrical spikes from neurons within the graft and align them to stimulus onset. In the visual cortical organoid protocol, locate the electrode track histologically, discard recordings within 100 μm of the graft–host border, and identify units whose firing clearly increases after light onset on a peri-stimulus time histogram.
milestones.set_by: Jgamadze and colleagues, published electrophysiology protocol in STAR Methods; written for visual cortical organoid grafts.
milestones.threshold_quote: PSTHs were manually reviewed to identify units that demonstrated a clear increase in firing following stimulus onset.

milestones.title: Residual undifferentiated cells in a stem cell-derived neuronal graft produce no tumors in animal testing.
milestones.criterion: In a long-term animal study of the final stem cell-derived product, show that residual undifferentiated cells do not form tumors. Run tumor-generating positive controls and negative controls for background tumors in parallel. Use the intended clinical implantation site when feasible and assess the proposed clinical dose or justify the animal dose.
milestones.set_by: International Society for Stem Cell Research, Guidelines section 3.3.2, especially Recommendation 3.3.2.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: the persistence of any remaining undifferentiated cells in the final product do not result in tumors.

milestones.title: A neuronal graft restores >70% of pre-lesion task accuracy, with recovery dependent on graft activity.
milestones.criterion: In large animals trained to >90% task accuracy, a lesion removes >80% of task ability. After graft maturation and retraining, accuracy exceeds 70% of pre-lesion accuracy and is one standard deviation above non-grafted controls. Imaging shows a healthy graft throughout. Silencing >50% of graft neurons causes a significant, transient accuracy decrease. A rat study published 6 April 2020 reversed forelimb asymmetry in 11 grafted rats, but silencing did not recreate that deficit; it does not satisfy this causal-recovery test.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H, FRONT solicitation Table 4, TA2b; thresholds appear only in a table and were written for neocortical grafts.

milestones.title: Both bemdaneprocel dose cohorts meet all four exPDite safety limits at one year.
milestones.criterion: At one year after transplantation, apply four limits separately to the low- and high-dose cohorts. At most two participants per cohort may experience two or more serious adverse events related to surgery, transplanted cells or immunosuppression. At most two may develop a graft-related tumor or abnormal tissue overgrowth, and at most two may develop a life-threatening intracerebral hemorrhage. At most one death may occur per cohort.
milestones.set_by: BlueRock Therapeutics and the exPDite investigators, NCT04802733, primary outcome in the published Methods.
milestones.threshold_quote: two or fewer participants in either cohort developing two or more SAEs related to surgery, the presence of transplanted cells or immunosuppression

milestones.title: Bemdaneprocel improves ON time without troublesome dyskinesia over sham surgery at week 78.
milestones.criterion: In the double-blind exPDite-2 trial, show a greater increase from baseline to week 78 with bemdaneprocel than with sham surgery in daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia, using a two-sided significance level of 0.05. Participants complete diaries on three consecutive days in the week before each visit. Sum the time when motor symptoms are controlled with either no involuntary movements or only non-troublesome ones, adjusted to a 16-hour waking day.
milestones.set_by: BlueRock Therapeutics, exPDite-2 (NCT06944522) published trial-design poster; written for Parkinson’s disease.
milestones.threshold_quote: Change from baseline to Week 78 in PD diary measure of ON time without troublesome dyskinesia

milestones.title: A dopamine progenitor lot meets all three MSK-DA01 protein-marker thresholds after thawing.
milestones.criterion: In the thawed day-16 MSK-DA01 product, intracellular flow cytometry finds more than 85% of cells positive for FOXA2, fewer than 5% positive for PAX6 and fewer than 0.2% positive for NANOG. These markers assess midbrain floor-plate identity, an unwanted early neural cell population and residual pluripotent cells, respectively.
milestones.set_by: Piao and colleagues, MSK-DA01 manufacturing and quality-assurance protocol.

milestones.title: A grafted marmoset reaches 27 correct choices in 30 on the same pre-graft object discrimination.
milestones.criterion: After a basal forebrain lesion, retest a previously learned two-object choice until the animal makes 27 correct choices in 30 trials. Three months after transplantation, present the same choice again. Record how many trials precede the qualifying block and compare the scores of grafted, lesion-only and unoperated animals. The number of additional trials distinguishes immediate performance from relearning.
milestones.set_by: Ridley and colleagues, marmoset visual-discrimination protocol, Tasks 6 and 7 and Table 1.

milestones.title: Large animals with cortical grafts regain more than 70% of pre-lesion task accuracy.
milestones.criterion: Train large animals to greater than 90% accuracy on a cortex-dependent task. The lesion must remove more than 80% of their ability to perform it. Noninvasive imaging must show a healthy graft throughout. After the graft matures and the animals are retrained, task accuracy must exceed 70% of pre-lesion accuracy and be one standard deviation above that of non-grafted controls.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H, FRONT solicitation, Table 4, TA2b, training and retraining rows.
milestones.threshold_quote: >70% reacquisition of task accuracy compared to pre-lesion

milestones.title: Silencing more than half the cortical graft neurons transiently reduces recovered task accuracy.
milestones.criterion: After large animals reacquire the cortex-dependent task, transiently block activity in more than 50% of graft neurons. Task accuracy must fall significantly during silencing and the decrease must be transient.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H, FRONT solicitation, Table 4, TA2b, graft function via silencing.
milestones.threshold_quote: significant – and transient – drop in task accuracy.

milestones.title: A blinded graft trial compares cognitive change with sham surgery at one year.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind comparison of bilateral dopamine-cell grafts and sham surgery for Parkinson’s disease, administer neuropsychological tests before surgery and one year afterward. Compare change between groups in verbal and visual memory and the other prespecified cognitive domains. This stage measures cognitive change without assigning a preservation margin.
milestones.set_by: Trott and colleagues, published protocol for cognitive assessment in the double-blind fetal dopamine-cell trial.
milestones.threshold_quote: were administered before and 1 year after surgery.

not_found: No validated preservation margin or follow-up interval for retained learning after neuronal grafting was found.
No large-animal result meeting the complete FRONT learned-task benchmark was located.
No randomized efficacy result for exPDite-2 was located.
ClinicalTrials.gov pages opened without study details; the sponsor’s trial-design poster and status page supplied the accessible information.
No combined human test for functional recovery and preservation of retained learning was found in FRONT, ISSCR guidance, the Japanese raguneprocel review or the Parkinson’s graft trials.

results.finding: Cortical grafts reversed cylinder-test forelimb asymmetry in 11 stroke-injured rats (P < 0.05 versus stroke-injured vehicle controls).
results.detail: The cylinder-test measure was the percentage of touches made with the impaired forelimb. The study did not measure accuracy relative to each animal’s pre-lesion baseline.
results.quote:
Cell transplantation completely
mitigated this behavioral asymmetry

results.finding: In 6 rats with halorhodopsin-expressing cortical grafts, illumination reduced cylinder-test forelimb touches bilaterally (P < 0.05).
results.detail: The decrease was in the number of touches. The recovered balance of left and right forelimb use persisted during illumination.
results.quote:
grafted neurons in vivo gave rise to bilateral reduction
of forelimb touches in the cylinder test

results.finding: Human cortical organoid grafts showed light-evoked firing in 6 of 8 adult rats tested.
results.quote:
Visually evoked neural ac-
tivity was detected for 6 of the 8 transplanted (0/1 at 1 mpt, 4/5 at
2 mpt, and 2/2 at 3 mpt) and both naive animals.

results.finding: Chemogenetic inhibition significantly reduced spontaneous cortical graft activity in an experiment with 2 adult rats.
results.detail: The outcome was spontaneous graft firing. The study did not measure task accuracy during or after inhibition.
results.quote:
While no change in the
neural activity of the brain was noted, a signiﬁcant decrease in
activity was observed in the organoid graft in response to CNO
administration ( Figures S7 S–S7U).

results.finding: In 7 mice with cortical human neural progenitor grafts, 2% of graft cells remained Ki67-positive at follow-up.
results.detail: The graft was implanted next to the cortical infarct. Nanog staining and Ki67 counts provide short-term evidence about cell identity and proliferation. Tumor formation requires a direct assessment over longer follow-up.
results.quote: whereas only 2% of grafted cells were identified to be Ki67-positive after 35 days

results.finding: Stroke-injured mice with cortical grafts (11 assigned per stroke arm) recovered better on the rotarod than vehicle controls (p = 0.0021).
results.detail: Rotarod performance was measured as latency to fall. The reported p-value does not establish recovery above 70% of baseline accuracy or a one-standard-deviation advantage over non-grafted controls.
results.quote:
Five weeks after stroke induction, mice that received NPCs showed an improved recovery in the rotarod test compared to the vehicle group (
p
= 0.0021, Supplementary Fig. 6B
).

results.finding: In 13 rats with fetal midbrain dopamine grafts, stepping recovery fell significantly 15 minutes after chemogenetic inhibition.
results.detail: The behavioral endpoints were forelimb use and adjusting steps. The study measured graft transduction and dopamine release, but did not quantify the fraction of graft neurons functionally silenced.
results.quote:
Thus, the
reversible inhibition obtained using SalB (in the Gq + KORD
rats) reinstated the behavioral deﬁcits in the stepping and cylin-
der tests.

results.finding: In human cortical organoid grafts in 3 rats, about 54% of 31 optotagged units increased firing after whisker stimulation.
results.detail: The authors compared firing during the second after whisker deflection with firing during the preceding second using a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
results.quote: approximately 54% of optotagged single units displayed significant increases in firing rates following whisker stimulation that peaked after approximately 650 ms

results.finding: Thawed PD01-04 dopaminergic grafts produced tumors in 0 of 27 NSG mice examined at day 274.
results.detail: Histology found no OCT4-positive cells in the unspiked grafts at days 29 and 274. The spiked controls demonstrated that the assay could detect tumors from undifferentiated cells.
results.quote: Importantly, all mice receiving PD01-04-mDACs survived until Day 274 without tumor formation.

results.finding: Across 25 MCB003-derived dopamine progenitor preparations, day-26 flow cytometry found a mean of 92.3% FOXA2/TUJ1 double-positive cells.
results.quote: We confirmed that 92.3% of the total cells are FOXA2+TUJ1+ DAPs on culture day 26.

results.finding: Of 80 NOG mice initially grafted with the final dopaminergic progenitor product, 0 had proliferative or malignant findings at terminal histology among those examined.
results.detail: Fifty-five graft recipients survived to week 52. Some grafts contained small, nonproliferating choroid plexus-like clusters.

results.finding: Four thawed MSK-DA01 lots met all marker limits, with FOXA2 positivity of at least 90.1%.
results.quote:
Data on thawed cells from MSK-DA01 showed a high percentage (90.1–94.4%) of FOXA2, a floor plate marker that is maintained throughout the development of mDA neurons, very low percentage of PAX6
+
(0.1–0.2%) and undetectable NANOG
+
cells (
Figure S1C
).

results.finding: Unspiked MSK-DA01 produced zero graft tumors in 38 analyzed NSG mice.
results.detail: Animals without surviving grafts were excluded from graft analysis. A primary neoplasm found at necropsy contained no human cells and was judged unrelated to the graft.
results.quote:
No tumors were observed in the grafts of the 100% MSK-DA01, 0.01% hESC or 0.1% hESC groups (
Figure 4B
–
D
).

results.finding: Among 12 bemdaneprocel recipients, 0 died through four years.
results.detail: The poster reports four-year follow-up for the low-dose (n=5) and high-dose (n=7) cohorts. Its introduction cites the earlier trial's overall 12-month safety result without giving the four threshold-specific results.
results.quote: No deaths, study discontinuations due to TEAEs, or graft-induced dyskinesias occurred

results.finding: High-dose bemdaneprocel recipients (n=7) gained a mean 1.0 hour of daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia at 48 months.
results.quote:
CFB in adjusted  PD diary ON time without troublesome dyskinesia at 48 months post -transplantation 
(mean [SD] hours) was  -0.1 [2.2] in the low-dose and 1.0 [2.7] in the high -dose group

results.finding: Bemdaneprocel recipients (n=12 across two dose cohorts) met all 4 prespecified one-year safety limits in each cohort.
results.quote: Predefined safety criteria for the primary outcome were satisfied at 12 months of follow-up after transplantation

results.finding: High-dose bemdaneprocel recipients (n=7) gained a mean 2.7 hours per day of ON time without troublesome dyskinesia at 18 months.
results.quote: The mean good ON times, based on adjusted PD diaries, increased by 0.2 h (3.8 h) from the baseline to 12.3 h (3.2 h) in the low-dose cohort and by 2.7 h (1.6 h) from the baseline to 13.6 h (1.9 h) in the high-dose cohort

results.finding: Among five macaques examined after neural precursor transplantation, zero showed graft overgrowth.
results.detail: The authors assessed overgrowth histologically in an efficacy study.
results.quote: no postgraft overgrowth was observed

results.finding: Of five grafted macaques analyzed, two underwent sham surgery, with no cognitive recovery after sham.
results.detail: The sham procedures were performed in animals that also received grafts. The cognitive outcome was performance on a detour task.
results.quote: No recovery from motor nor from nonmotor cognitive and circadian symptoms was observed following sham surgery

results.finding: Adult macaques with cortical biopsy-derived cell grafts (n=2 newly treated) recovered up to 92% of their pre-lesion timed pellet count.
results.detail: The outcome was the number of pellets retrieved in 30 seconds. The graft consisted of cultured cells from a prefrontal cortical biopsy. Postmortem fluorescence was lost, leaving graft fate and integration unresolved.
results.quote: Their second post‐lesion plateau for the total score reached 67% and 92% (with respect to pre‐lesion score), corresponding to a rebound of recovery of 17% and 27% in Mk‐CA and Mk‐LO, respectively (see also Figure  4 ).

results.finding: AMCHEPRY with undifferentiated iPS cells at the specification limit produced 0 graft-related tumors or teratomas in NOG mice (group sizes unreported).
results.detail: Systemic neoplasms in mice that died in the AMCHEPRY group were Ku80-negative and judged spontaneous. The exact iPS-cell spike count is redacted.
results.quote: no tumor formation or teratoma formation was observed up to 39  weeks of observation

results.finding: No tumors were detected at 48 weeks in rats with human iPSC-derived cortical progenitor grafts (tumor-screening n unspecified).
results.detail: A separate graft-survival assessment found viable grafts in 7 of 9 rats at 8–10 months. That sample size cannot be assigned to the tumor screen.
results.quote: Notably, neither whole-body FDG PET-CT nor H&E staining detected any evidence of tumor formation at the 12-month post-transplantation mark

results.finding: Mouse ESC-derived basal forebrain cholinergic progenitor grafts produced 0 detectable brain tumors in 42 analyzed Alzheimer’s model mice.
results.detail: Sham and ungrafted groups served as behavioral controls. The excerpt reports no tumor endpoint for the human ESC-derived grafts.
results.quote:
There was no detectable sign of tumor formation in host
brains grafted with BFCN progenitor cells in the NBM.

case_label = "Replacement target". Reason: The replacement target determines what anatomical and functional result a graft must achieve.

definition = "Living replacement neurons join surviving brain circuits and help restore a function lost to injury or neurodegeneration. A person may need to relearn the lost skill. Preservation concerns skills the person could still perform just before transplantation and can still perform afterward. Japan has conditionally approved raguneprocel, a graft of immature dopamine-producing nerve cells, for a limited period for Parkinson\u2019s motor symptoms inadequately controlled by medication. Preservation of learned skills remains a separate question.". Reason: The definition needs to distinguish retaining an available skill from relearning a lost one and to identify the closest clinical use.

goal.need = "More than 20 million US adults are estimated to live with chronic damage to the neocortex after stroke, trauma or neurodegeneration. Physical and speech therapy can improve function, but people with severe damage often depend on caregivers. Replacing lost neurons could help someone regain speech, vision or control of movement while keeping skills they still use in daily life. Recovery may still require practice specific to the lost skill.". Reason: The current passage mentions a population estimate without giving the number or explaining what recovery would mean for patients.

edit completion: basis = "The ISSCR calls for controlled evidence of effectiveness. FRONT measures reacquisition of a learned task in animals. Japan\u2019s conditional approval of raguneprocel concerns Parkinson\u2019s motor symptoms and requires further efficacy assessment. A sham-controlled trial of fetal dopamine grafts compared cognitive performance before surgery and one year later. Its nonsignificant group difference does not bound the amount of decline compatible with the data. The combined test and its requirement for a justified preservation margin are Atlas criteria."; refs = [1, 4, 19, 22, 23]. Reason: The basis omits both a controlled human study of cognition after grafting and a regulatory decision limited to motor symptoms.
add case "Neocortical tissue". Reason: FRONT tests reconstruction of organized neocortical tissue after damage to a cortical area.
add case "Midbrain dopamine neurons". Reason: The Parkinson’s trials aim to restore dopamine input to the striatum and use indication-specific motor endpoints.
add case "Basal forebrain cholinergic neurons". Reason: The marmoset retention experiment replaced cholinergic input to surviving cortex after damage to the basal forebrain.

add milestone after None: "A dopamine progenitor lot meets all three MSK-DA01 protein-marker thresholds after thawing.". Reason: The milestones begin after transplantation and omit the laboratory test that identifies dopamine progenitors suitable for graft studies.

edit m1: criterion = "Record electrical spikes from neurons within the graft and align them to stimulus onset. In the visual cortical organoid protocol, locate the electrode track histologically, discard recordings within 100 \u03bcm of the graft\u2013host border, and identify units whose firing clearly increases after light onset on a peri-stimulus time histogram.". Reason: The criterion mixes the visual-response test with the number of animals that passed it.

edit m2: title = "Residual undifferentiated cells in a stem cell-derived neuronal graft produce no tumors in animal testing."; criterion = "In a long-term animal study of the final stem cell-derived product, show that residual undifferentiated cells do not form tumors. Run tumor-generating positive controls and negative controls for background tumors in parallel. Use the intended clinical implantation site when feasible and assess the proposed clinical dose or justify the animal dose."; refs = [4, 7]. Reason: The ISSCR criterion should specify what validates a negative tumor finding without treating one mouse study’s duration or allocation as part of the test.

add milestone after m2: "A grafted marmoset reaches 27 correct choices in 30 on the same pre-graft object discrimination.". Reason: The existing animal milestones never retest a specific skill demonstrated after injury and before transplantation.

split m3 into "Large animals with cortical grafts regain more than 70% of pre-lesion task accuracy." | "Silencing more than half the cortical graft neurons transiently reduces recovered task accuracy.". Reason: FRONT Table 4 scores task reacquisition and the subsequent causal test by graft silencing in separate rows.

edit m4: title = "Both bemdaneprocel dose cohorts meet all four exPDite safety limits at one year."; criterion = "At one year after transplantation, apply four limits separately to the low- and high-dose cohorts. At most two participants per cohort may experience two or more serious adverse events related to surgery, transplanted cells or immunosuppression. At most two may develop a graft-related tumor or abnormal tissue overgrowth, and at most two may develop a life-threatening intracerebral hemorrhage. At most one death may occur per cohort."; set_by = "BlueRock Therapeutics and the exPDite investigators, NCT04802733, primary outcome in the published Methods."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "two or fewer participants in either cohort developing two or more SAEs related to surgery, the presence of transplanted cells or immunosuppression"; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9]. Reason: The phase I publication gives four numerical safety limits by cohort that the existing criterion omits.

add milestone after m4: "A blinded graft trial compares cognitive change with sham surgery at one year.". Reason: The human milestones track safety and motor benefit but omit the controlled preoperative and postoperative assessment of cognition already used in graft recipients.

edit m5: title = "Bemdaneprocel improves ON time without troublesome dyskinesia over sham surgery at week 78."; criterion = "In the double-blind exPDite-2 trial, show a greater increase from baseline to week 78 with bemdaneprocel than with sham surgery in daily ON time without troublesome dyskinesia, using a two-sided significance level of 0.05. Participants complete diaries on three consecutive days in the week before each visit. Sum the time when motor symptoms are controlled with either no involuntary movements or only non-troublesome ones, adjusted to a 16-hour waking day."; refs = [10]. Reason: The recruitment date and power assumption obscure the actual week-78 comparison and its diary collection period.
remove not found 4. Reason: The full 2016 Neuron paper is accessible and reports selective modulation of graft function in rats.
